analysis.title: Enphase Energy Inc. (ENPH): Cost reset not surprising given uncertain macro and slower growth into 2027
key_insights: ENPH announced a restructuring with a ~12% workforce reduction (~320 employees), relocation of functions to lower cost regions and consolidation of manufacturing and facilities.
Non-GAAP opex is targeted at $60-$65mn per quarter from 1Q27 versus ~$80mn currently, a ~$15-$20mn quarterly reduction.
4Q26 guidance is unchanged except for ~$24mn restructuring and impairment charge in GAAP opex.

Management said market conditions were more challenging than expected, citing expiry of the 30% residential 25D tax credit, elevated rates and European uncertainty and competition. US sell-through fell 35% yoy in 3Q26.
GS sees the restructuring as a cost reset to an already weak demand backdrop, not a signal of further near-term deterioration. 2027 focus shifts to the pace of demand recovery.
Total restructuring charges are $25-$28mn, with only ~$13mn in cash, modest relative to the savings.
GS keeps Buy and cuts the 12m PT to $36 from $40, using a 15.0X P/E (from 18.0X, lower comps) on Q5-Q8 EPS plus $7/share net cash (from $8). Implied upside is 83.4% from $19.63.
GS raises EPS to $1.62/$1.60/$2.34 for 2026E/2027E/2028E (0%/+11%/+6%) on lower costs. 2027E revenue is cut 2% to $977.0mn and 2028E 3% to $1,198.5mn.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $36 from $40 on a lower target multiple of 15.0X, while the cost reset supports earnings on a lower revenue base.

sector_views.rationale: Resi solar trends are challenging into 2027 after the 25D credit expiry, with high rates and weak US sell-through.

earnings_insights: 4Q26 guidance maintained, excluding ~$24mn restructuring and impairment charge in GAAP opex (company guidance).
GS non-GAAP EPS estimates (diluted): 2026E $1.62 unchanged, 2027E $1.60 (prior $1.44), 2028E $2.34 (prior $2.21). 2025 EPS was $2.97 per the summary table.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.28, 1Q27E $0.19, 2Q27E $0.33. 3Q26 EPS was $0.41.
risk_factors: Changes in the competitive and technology landscape.
Abnormal inventory builds across the channel.
Weaker residential demand after 25D credit expiry and elevated rates, plus competition in Europe.
geopolitical: US-China tariffs are flagged as a key risk for ENPH.
